evidence_use.operator: arithmetic means and sample SDs on complete endpoint pairs
evidence_use.population: 12 adult men aged 35-55 with abdominal overweight/obesity; fasting measurements before/after 3 days at approximately 50% usual energy intake; no control arm.
evidence_use.measurement: Units specified per endpoint; serum leptin is raw ng/mL, not a log transformation
evidence_use.reason: Use each rounded arithmetic mean and sample SD as a plug-in population marginal parameter, with lognormal parameters solved analytically. Outputs retain raw measurement units, including raw leptin. These are target-derived reconstruction inputs, not independent validation evidence. Cohort moments fluctuate and parameter uncertainty and rounding uncertainty are not modeled; the supplied SD is not paired-change variability.

evidence_use.population: 12 adult men aged 35-55 with abdominal overweight/obesity; fasting measurements before/after 3 days at approximately 50% usual energy intake; no control arm.
evidence_use.reason: Represent one pre/post pair per synthetic person with exactly the supplied endpoint complete-pair counts scaled to n. All four endpoints are complete in this packet. Eligibility and the intervention define the intended population and visit interpretation; no unprovided age, adiposity, intake or control-arm variables are invented.

components.name: positive_raw_marginals
components.source_to_target_assumptions: Same-population A0 reconstruction. The positive lognormal family is a modeling assumption, not supplied shape evidence. For each mean m and SD s, log variance is log(1+(s/m)^2), and log mean is log(m) minus half that variance. This reproduces population arithmetic moments, not exact small-cohort sample moments.

components.name: stable_person_dependence
components.source_to_target_assumptions: A common normal person factor has variance weight 0.20, an independent endpoint-specific stable person factor has weight 0.70, and independent visit fluctuations have weight 0.10. The resulting latent normal correlations are 0.90 within an endpoint and 0.20 across endpoints at either visit. Stability over a short paired interval motivates this simple shared structure; every numerical weight is explicitly assumed and is not estimated from the packet. No shared intervention-response factor, treatment-effect heterogeneity distribution, or direction constraint on individual changes is claimed as known.

components.name: counts_keys_and_randomness
components.source_to_target_assumptions: n denotes persons; each complete-pair count is round(packet endpoint n times requested n divided by packet person count). If generalized inputs introduce missing pairs, their synthetic positions are sampled without replacement independently by endpoint, an unvalidated missing-completely-at-random convention. This packet introduces none. New synthetic keys incorporate the input seed and row number. Only a local numpy default_rng is used and evidence is read without mutation.

scenarios.assumption: One fixed lognormal factor model with latent within-endpoint correlation 0.90 and cross-endpoint correlation 0.20. These are transparent working assumptions, not inferred correlations or evidence of correct uncertainty coverage.
scenarios.inclusion_rationale: Retain the supplied positive-support stochastic model because the source-only feedback identifies no defect and the available marginals do not discriminate dependence alternatives. The no-op was selected before branch verification. All three scheduled seeds are used without seed selection. The 20-cohort allocation is a computational resource allocation, not a posterior probability.
unresolved_dependencies: All four actual within-person pre/post covariances and change SDs are unknown.
All cross-endpoint covariances, including the six change correlations, are unknown.
Tail shape, individual response heterogeneity and uncertainty in the rounded small-sample marginal estimates are unknown.
No control arm permits an independently validated causal effect interpretation.
affected_analysis_classes: Four paired endpoint change means and paired t intervals: marginal mean differences are reconstruction inputs, whereas finite-cohort means and interval widths depend on assumed sampling and pairing.
Paired covariance and change-SD diagnostics depend on the assumed lognormal factor structure.
Six correlations between endpoint changes depend on assumed shared-person factors, marginal transformations and visit fluctuations.
scenarios.scientific_scenario_differences: One retained target scenario; there is no scientific change from the parent and no retained alternative.
